description: Step 5 display model derived from tbl_Risks.json + tbl_Harmonised_Standards.json. Each risk carries its category applicability question (Step A) and its requirement areas / subcategory treatment questions (Step B). Edit wording here to adapt the Step 5 screen.

wizard_questions.question:
User Documentation: Do system operators need documentation to understand any of the following?
a) What the system is capable of doing
b) The system's known limitations or blind spots
c) Instructions for proper and safe usage

Human Oversight: Do users interact with the system in a way that requires any of the following?
a) Relying on the system to make or inform decisions
b) The ability to understand and interpret the outputs
c) The ability to override decisions or safely halt operations

Cybersecurity: Is the system exposed to any of the following attack vectors?
a) External or untrusted users
b) Third-party data or models
c) Public or networked infrastructure

Accuracy: Do any of the following apply to the system's outputs?
a) Produces predictions
b) Produces classifications
c) Supports a task where output correctness is critical

wizard_questions.risk_name: Fragile or unsafe behaviour under stress
wizard_questions.question:
Robustness: Must the system remain stable when facing any of the following?
a) Corrupted or unexpected inputs
b) Changing environmental conditions
c) Adversarial inputs or usage

Data Quality: Do any of the following apply to the system's datasets?
a) Performance depends on data quality or selection
b) Uses data for training or fine-tuning
c) Uses data for retrieval (RAG)
d) Provenance and origin of the data affect outputs

Bias & Fairness: Do any of the following apply to the system?
a) Processes personal data about individuals
b) Makes or informs decisions affecting people
c) Could inadvertently treat demographic groups (age, gender, ethnicity, etc.) differently

Logging: Does the system require a secure, unalterable audit trail for any of the following?
a) System inputs and prompts
b) Automated decisions and outputs
c) System events and errors

Traceability: Must past system events be reconstructable for any of the following reasons?
a) Routine audits or compliance checks
b) Incident investigations or failure analysis
c) Human oversight reviews

Quality Management (QMS): Does your organization's role include any of the following?
a) Acting as the original provider of a high-risk AI system
b) Making substantial modifications to an existing AI system
c) Operating under a formal Quality Management System

Risk Management: Does the system require risk management for any of the following phases?
a) Initial design and development
b) Continuous monitoring during its active lifecycle
c) Documented mitigation of known and emerging risks

Technical Documentation: Do you need to produce a formal Technical File detailing any of the following?
a) How the system was designed and built
b) How the system was validated and tested
c) How the system is version-controlled

System Modifications: Will the system undergo future updates involving any of the following?
a) New models or significant architecture changes
b) New retrieval data or training datasets
c) Changes to the system's intended purpose

Deployer Obligations: Does your organization's responsibility include any of the following?
a) Acting as the deployer of a high-risk AI system
b) Managing the system's day-to-day operation in production
c) Ensuring the system is used according to the provider's instructions

Conformity Assessment: Is the system subject to any of the following pre-launch requirements?
a) Being formally placed on the EU market
b) Being put into service for its intended use
c) Requiring a formal conformity assessment

Transparency & Content Labeling: Does the system do any of the following?
a) Simulate human interaction
b) Generate synthetic content (text, images, audio, video)
c) Manipulate content shown to users

Post-Market Monitoring: Will the live system require continuous monitoring to detect any of the following?
a) Performance drift or data shifts
b) System degradation over time
c) Safety incidents or unexpected risks

Opaque system to deployers.article_name: Article 13: Transparency and Provision of Information to Deployers
Opaque system to deployers.category_question:
User Documentation: Do system operators need documentation to understand any of the following?
a) What the system is capable of doing
b) The system's known limitations or blind spots
c) Instructions for proper and safe usage
Opaque system to deployers.risk_description: Opaque system to deployers — deployers lack the purpose, limitations and instructions needed to use the system correctly.

areas.treatment_question:
User Instructions: Do the people using the system require any of the following?
a) Clear instructions on what the system is for
b) Warnings on when not to rely on it
c) Guidance on how to use it safely

Ineffective human oversight.category_question:
Human Oversight: Do users interact with the system in a way that requires any of the following?
a) Relying on the system to make or inform decisions
b) The ability to understand and interpret the outputs
c) The ability to override decisions or safely halt operations
Ineffective human oversight.risk_description: Ineffective human oversight — people cannot understand, question or halt the outputs, so they over-rely on the system.

areas.treatment_question:
Human Oversight: Do people acting on the system's outputs need any of the following?
a) Prompts to prevent over-trusting the AI
b) A mechanism to override decisions or halt operations
c) Sufficient explanation to understand the system's reasoning

Security compromise.category_question:
Cybersecurity: Is the system exposed to any of the following attack vectors?
a) External or untrusted users
b) Third-party data or models
c) Public or networked infrastructure
Security compromise.risk_description: Security compromise — the model, its data or its pipelines are attacked, corrupted or accessed without authorisation.

areas.treatment_question:
Threat Vulnerability: Is the system vulnerable to attackers attempting any of the following?
a) Feeding crafted inputs to fool the logic (evasion)
b) Poisoning the training or retrieval data
c) Probing to steal the model or underlying data

Supply Chain Integrity: Does the system rely on any of the following that could be tampered with?
a) Custom code or infrastructure
b) Data or deployment pipelines
c) Third-party models, components, or libraries

Access Security: Does the system require any of the following security measures?
a) Locking down access to model weights
b) Restricting access to underlying data and admin functions
c) Hardening the model to resist external manipulation

Active Detection: Does the system need active monitoring to detect any of the following in real-time?
a) Prompt injection attacks
b) Malicious probing or anomalous behavior
c) Evasion attempts bypassing preventative controls

Inaccurate or unproven performance.category_question:
Accuracy: Do any of the following apply to the system's outputs?
a) Produces predictions
b) Produces classifications
c) Supports a task where output correctness is critical
Inaccurate or unproven performance.risk_description: Inaccurate or unproven performance — accuracy is not measured, validated, declared or monitored, so the system performs worse than believed.

areas.treatment_question:
Accuracy Testing: Does the system's output accuracy require any of the following?
a) Formal measurement using appropriate statistical metrics
b) Rigorous testing on unseen validation datasets
c) Explicit declaration of the achieved accuracy results

Performance Drift: Once live, does the system require any of the following to maintain accuracy?
a) Continuous monitoring for performance drift
b) Ongoing benchmarking against baselines
c) Alerts when accuracy falls below acceptable thresholds

Validation Documentation: Does the system require formal documentation for any of the following?
a) How the accuracy was statistically tested
b) The methodology behind the train/test data split
c) The specific validation methods used to verify results

Fragile or unsafe behaviour under stress.category_question:
Robustness: Must the system remain stable when facing any of the following?
a) Corrupted or unexpected inputs
b) Changing environmental conditions
c) Adversarial inputs or usage
Fragile or unsafe behaviour under stress.risk_description: Fragile or unsafe behaviour under stress — the system fails unpredictably on noisy, shifting or adversarial conditions, or emits unsafe content.

areas.treatment_question:
Operational Robustness: Must the system continue operating safely when encountering any of the following?
a) Messy, corrupted, or unexpected inputs
b) Rapidly changing environmental conditions
c) Feedback loops that could degrade performance

Fail-Safe Mechanisms: In the event of a failure, must the system execute any of the following?
a) Graceful degradation of functionality
b) Fall back to a predefined safe state
c) Avoid unpredictable or abrupt collapse

Reproducibility: Does the system's reliability depend on any of the following?
a) Producing consistent, deterministic outputs
b) Generating the exact same response for the same input
c) Eliminating random or unpredictable variations

Content Safety: Does the system require moderation guardrails to prevent any of the following?
a) Displaying toxic or abusive content to users
b) Generating harmful or dangerous instructions
c) Bypassing safety filters via prompt injection

Poor data quality & governance.category_question:
Data Quality: Do any of the following apply to the system's datasets?
a) Performance depends on data quality or selection
b) Uses data for training or fine-tuning
c) Uses data for retrieval (RAG)
d) Provenance and origin of the data affect outputs
Poor data quality & governance.risk_description: Poor data quality & governance — the data driving the system is undocumented, unrepresentative, incomplete, inaccurate or unlawfully retained.

areas.treatment_question:
Data Provenance: Does the data governance process require documentation for any of the following?
a) The origin and provenance of the data
b) The rationale for choosing specific datasets
c) The specific methods used for data preparation and cleaning

Data Quality Metrics: Does the system's data quality require measurement of any of the following?
a) How representative the data is of the target environment
b) The completeness of the records (lack of data gaps)
c) The accuracy and correctness of the labels and raw data

Data Lifecycle Rules: Does the system require strict rules governing any of the following?
a) How datasets are split (training, validation, testing)
b) How long the data is retained for compliance
c) The secure decommissioning of expired data

Data Formulation: Must the project explicitly document any of the following?
a) The core assumptions about what the data represents
b) What the data is intended to measure or predict
c) The contextual limitations of the data sources

Privacy Egress: Does the system require egress filtering to prevent any of the following?
a) Personal data leaking into prompts or outputs
b) Confidential information leaving your controlled environment
c) External models retaining or training on your submitted data

Discriminatory or biased outcomes.category_question:
Bias & Fairness: Do any of the following apply to the system?
a) Processes personal data about individuals
b) Makes or informs decisions affecting people
c) Could inadvertently treat demographic groups (age, gender, ethnicity, etc.) differently
Discriminatory or biased outcomes.risk_description: Discriminatory or biased outcomes — unfair results across groups because bias in the data or model is not detected or mitigated.

areas.treatment_question:
Bias & Proxy Detection: Does the system require checks to prevent bias involving any of the following?
a) Disparate impacts on protected demographic groups
b) Hidden proxy variables (e.g., zip code acting as a stand-in for ethnicity)
c) Under-representation of specific groups in the data

Fairness Definition: Does defining "fairness" for the system require any of the following?
a) Gathering input from diverse, multi-stakeholder teams
b) Consulting with the people directly affected by the system
c) Linking mitigation measures directly to fundamental rights

Incomplete event recording.category_question:
Logging: Does the system require a secure, unalterable audit trail for any of the following?
a) System inputs and prompts
b) Automated decisions and outputs
c) System events and errors
Incomplete event recording.risk_description: Incomplete event recording — the system does not immutably record the events needed to reconstruct what happened.

areas.treatment_question:
Event Reconstruction: Must the system maintain permanent records of any of the following?
a) The specific inputs or prompts received
b) The automated decisions or outputs generated
c) Sufficient detail to fully reconstruct a past event

Inadequate system logging.category_question:
Traceability: Must past system events be reconstructable for any of the following reasons?
a) Routine audits or compliance checks
b) Incident investigations or failure analysis
c) Human oversight reviews
Inadequate system logging.risk_description: Inadequate system logging — the system does not automatically record the events, inputs, states and errors needed to reconstruct and audit its behaviour.

areas.treatment_question:
Automated Logging: Does the system require automated logging for any of the following?
a) Key performance benchmarks or safety checks
b) System errors, crashes, or fallback activations
c) Every instance where a human overrides or stops the system

Log Completeness: Must the system's logs capture any of the following details?
a) The system's state and active model version at the time
b) The specific retrieved data or context behind a decision
c) Detailed diagnostic data and error codes

Log Governance: Do the system's logs require any of the following governance controls?
a) Tamper-proof storage (e.g., cryptographic hashes, WORM storage)
b) Enforcement of minimum retention periods
c) Privacy protections (e.g., data minimization or anonymization)

No quality management system.category_question:
Quality Management (QMS): Does your organization's role include any of the following?
a) Acting as the original provider of a high-risk AI system
b) Making substantial modifications to an existing AI system
c) Operating under a formal Quality Management System
No quality management system.risk_description: No quality management system — the organisation lacks the documented QMS to keep the AI conformant over its life.

areas.treatment_question:
Provider Strategy: As the provider, does your organization require any of the following?
a) A formally documented compliance strategy
b) Clear accountability and defined management roles
c) A structured framework for maintaining ongoing conformity

Development Controls: Does your organization require established procedures for any of the following?
a) Controlling system design and development
b) Verification and validation testing
c) Managing human and technical resources (e.g., compute power)

Post-Launch Duties: Once the system is launched, do you require standing procedures for any of the following?
a) Continuous post-market monitoring of the system
b) Reporting serious incidents to national authorities
c) Adhering to strict regulatory reporting timelines

Record Retention: Are you required to maintain any of the following for the system's lifespan?
a) The comprehensive Technical File (Annex IV)
b) Version-controlled architecture documentation
c) Long-term storage of logs and compliance records

Unmanaged risk lifecycle.category_question:
Risk Management: Does the system require risk management for any of the following phases?
a) Initial design and development
b) Continuous monitoring during its active lifecycle
c) Documented mitigation of known and emerging risks
Unmanaged risk lifecycle.risk_description: Unmanaged risk lifecycle — the system's risks are not systematically identified, evaluated and mitigated across its life.

areas.treatment_question:
Risk Iteration: Does this high-risk system require a risk management process that includes any of the following?
a) Identifying known and reasonably foreseeable risks
b) Estimating and evaluating the severity of those risks
c) Continuously revisiting the evaluation as new data emerges

Mitigation Hierarchy: Must identified risks be mitigated using any of the following steps?
a) Eliminating the risk entirely through system design
b) Implementing technical controls to reduce unavoidable risks
c) Flagging any residual risk through adequate user information

Incomplete technical file.category_question:
Technical Documentation: Do you need to produce a formal Technical File detailing any of the following?
a) How the system was designed and built
b) How the system was validated and tested
c) How the system is version-controlled
Incomplete technical file.risk_description: Incomplete technical file — identity, architecture, training, performance and change history are not documented to a reviewable standard.

areas.treatment_question:
System Description: Does the technical documentation need to cover any of the following?
a) A clear declaration of the system's identity and intended purpose
b) A description of the architecture and component interactions
c) The specific methodologies and algorithms used for training

Performance Evidence: Must the system's performance records include any of the following?
a) The specific accuracy levels and metrics achieved
b) A summary of the testing and validation outcomes
c) The conditions and datasets used during testing

Change Management: Because the system will evolve, do you require any of the following?
a) A strict version control scheme for all releases
b) Traceability between system versions and their documentation
c) An auditable log of all modifications made after launch

Unmanaged substantial modification.category_question:
System Modifications: Will the system undergo future updates involving any of the following?
a) New models or significant architecture changes
b) New retrieval data or training datasets
c) Changes to the system's intended purpose
Unmanaged substantial modification.risk_description: Unmanaged substantial modification — changes aren't evaluated for whether they trigger re-assessment or shift provider responsibility.

areas.treatment_question:
Modification Assessment: When modifying the system, must you evaluate any of the following?
a) Whether the modification qualifies as "substantial" under the AI Act
b) Whether the change affects the system's core compliance
c) Whether the modification shifts legal Provider responsibilities to you

Re-conformity: If a substantial change occurs, does it require any of the following actions?
a) Triggering a full or partial re-run of the conformity assessment
b) Updating the Technical File and architecture documentation
c) Re-evaluating performance evidence and modification logs

Unmet deployer duties.category_question:
Deployer Obligations: Does your organization's responsibility include any of the following?
a) Acting as the deployer of a high-risk AI system
b) Managing the system's day-to-day operation in production
c) Ensuring the system is used according to the provider's instructions
Unmet deployer duties.risk_description: Unmet deployer duties — the deployer doesn't operate per instructions, implement oversight, monitor/log, or assess affected persons.

areas.treatment_question:
Deployer Governance: As the deployer, are you responsible for any of the following?
a) Operating the system strictly within its intended purpose and instructions
b) Assigning competent personnel to perform human oversight
c) Monitoring system operation and retaining logs

Impact Assessment: Prior to deployment, does your use case require any of the following?
a) Conducting a fundamental rights impact assessment
b) Documenting the findings and notifying the provider of risks
c) Identifying the specific categories of people affected by the outputs

Unverified conformity.category_question:
Conformity Assessment: Is the system subject to any of the following pre-launch requirements?
a) Being formally placed on the EU market
b) Being put into service for its intended use
c) Requiring a formal conformity assessment
Unverified conformity.risk_description: Unverified conformity — the system is deployed without a completed, signed-off conformity assessment.

areas.treatment_question:
Pre-Market Review: Before the system goes live, do you require any of the following internal reviews?
a) Verification that all applicable Article 9-17 controls are assessed
b) Confirmation that evidence exists for every applicable requirement
c) Formal sign-off by a reviewer with sufficient technical and legal competence

Conformity Conclusion: Must the conformity assessment conclude with any of the following?
a) A formal declaration that no critical compliance gaps remain
b) Confirmation that all identified gaps were resolved prior to market placement
c) A documented conclusion statement confirming regulatory compliance

Assessment Record: Must the final conformity record capture any of the following details?
a) The exact date the conformity assessment was completed
b) The specific version of the system that was assessed
c) The version of the compliance framework used for the evaluation

Undisclosed AI interaction or content.article_name: Article 50: Transparency Obligations for Certain AI Systems
Undisclosed AI interaction or content.category_question:
Transparency & Content Labeling: Does the system do any of the following?
a) Simulate human interaction
b) Generate synthetic content (text, images, audio, video)
c) Manipulate content shown to users
Undisclosed AI interaction or content.risk_description: Undisclosed AI interaction or content — people aren't told they're dealing with AI, or AI-generated content isn't labelled.

areas.treatment_question:
AI Identity Disclosure: Does the system interact with users in a way that requires any of the following?
a) A clear, timely disclosure that they are interacting with an AI
b) A notification presented before any consequential output is produced
c) Disclosures written in plain language accessible to the audience

Synthetic Content Labelling: Does the system generate or manipulate content requiring any of the following?
a) Machine-readable labels identifying it as AI-generated
b) Visible watermarks or markers for end users
c) Provenance metadata to support downstream deep fake detection

Deployer Duties (Transparency): As the deployer, are you required to ensure any of the following regarding disclosures?
a) Implementing the provider's transparency instructions
b) Keeping the AI identity disclosure active in the live production environment
c) Testing the disclosure mechanism for visibility and accessibility

Blind post-market operation.category_question:
Post-Market Monitoring: Will the live system require continuous monitoring to detect any of the following?
a) Performance drift or data shifts
b) System degradation over time
c) Safety incidents or unexpected risks
Blind post-market operation.risk_description: Blind post-market operation — the live system isn't monitored, so drift, degradation and incidents go undetected.

areas.treatment_question:
Post-Market Monitoring (PMM): Once the system is live, does your post-market monitoring require any of the following?
a) A documented plan defining the scope and frequency of reviews
b) Active collection of accuracy metrics, error rates, and user feedback
c) Automated checks to detect model drift or data distribution shifts

Feedback Loops & Correction: Does the system's feedback loop require any of the following?
a) A clear channel for users and affected persons to report incidents
b) A mechanism for logging and reviewing unexpected behavior or near-misses
c) A documented corrective action process to remediate reported issues
